title: The right adjoint for an open immersion
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, including the
finite coefficient rings
$A_{E,n}$,
and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a
open immersion.
On the small pro-etale sites,
extension by zero has the
inverse image as its
right adjoint on the entire ordinary derived categories:

$$
j_!:D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\rightleftarrows
D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):j^*.
$$

In particular, the right adjoint is constructed without a constructibility
or finite-Tor hypothesis.

proof.text: For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1)-(3) identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, identifies $A_U$ with the restriction of $A_X$, and gives restriction of module sheaves. To identify this restriction with the canonical inverse image, use the explicit definition [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For an object $V\to U$, its inverse-image indexing category $\mathcal I_V$ has initial object $(V\to X,\ (V\to U,\mathrm{id}_V):V\to U\times_XV)$: the unique arrow from it to $(T,\phi)$ is the projection $a:V\xrightarrow{\phi}U\times_XT\to T$. Indeed, the first projection of $\phi$ is the fixed map $V\to U$, since both have the same composite to $X$ and $j$ is a monomorphism by localization clause (4); hence $(\mathrm{id}_U\times_Xa)\circ(V\to U,\mathrm{id}_V)=\phi$. The second projection also forces uniqueness of $a$. Thus $\mathcal I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$ has a terminal object and the defining colimit is $N(V\to X)$. These identifications commute with restriction maps, and restriction is already a sheaf by the identified coverings, so the final sheafification changes nothing. Applying this to the underlying abelian sheaf and its action identifies module inverse image with restriction. On constant sections the canonical coefficient map sends $a$ to $a$; write $b:A_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X|_U$ for localization clause (2). Under the computed inverse-image identification, the canonical coefficient map $c:A_X|_U\to A_U$ fixes constants, so $bc$ fixes constants and equals the identity, by the sheafification universal property of the constant sheaf. Thus $c=b^{-1}$, giving precisely $j^{-1}A_X\cong A_U$. This supplies precisely the ring-sheaf identification for module pullback, for the given arbitrary finite commutative $A$. Put $F=j_!$ and $G=j^*$. The sheaf-level adjunction [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] supplies natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,GN)$. Exactness of $F$ is [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]; additive exact module inverse image along the open immersion is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Thus $F$ and $G$ form an additive exact adjoint pair on the full categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves.

proof.text: Apply $F,G$ termwise to unbounded cochain complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](a)-(b), their degreewise unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ are natural chain maps satisfying the triangle identities, and the same adjunction holds on homotopy categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors $\overline F,\overline G$ on the ordinary derived categories with natural comparison isomorphisms $\overline FQ_U\cong Q_XF$ and $\overline GQ_X\cong Q_UG$. Write these comparisons as $p_M:\overline FQ_UM\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XFM$ and $q_N:\overline GQ_XN\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_UGN$. The composite comparisons are $q_{FM}\circ\overline G(p_M)$ and $p_{GN}\circ\overline F(q_N)$, respectively. Use these comparisons and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to descend $Q_U\eta$ and $Q_X\varepsilon$ to $\overline\eta:\mathrm{id}\to\overline G\overline F$ and $\overline\varepsilon:\overline F\overline G\to\mathrm{id}$. Explicitly, $\overline\eta_{Q_UM}=(q_{FM}\circ\overline G(p_M))^{-1}\circ Q_U(\eta_M)$ and $\overline\varepsilon_{Q_XN}=Q_X(\varepsilon_N)\circ p_{GN}\circ\overline F(q_N)$. At $Q_UM$, the composite $\overline\varepsilon_{\overline FQ_UM}\circ\overline F(\overline\eta_{Q_UM})$, under the displayed comparisons, is $Q_X(\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M)=\mathrm{id}_{Q_XFM}$. At $Q_XN$, the other triangle is $Q_U(G\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{GN})=\mathrm{id}_{Q_UGN}$. For the first identity, naturality of $\overline\varepsilon$ along $p_M$ moves its evaluation from $\overline FQ_UM$ to $Q_XFM$; substitution of the two component formulas cancels $\overline F(q_{FM})$ and its inverse, and naturality of $p$ along $\eta_M$ leaves $Q_X(\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M)$. For the second, naturality of $\overline\eta$ along $q_N$ and of $q$ along $\varepsilon_N$ cancels $\overline G(p_{GN})$ and its inverse and leaves $Q_U(G\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{GN})$. These are the original triangle identities; part (3) of the localization universal property extends the identities from images of complexes to the derived functors themselves. Hence $\overline F\dashv\overline G$. The exact-functor characterization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor](1) makes these their left and right derived functors. Finally [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with $R_X=A_X$, $R_U=A_U$ and the ring identification from step 1, defines $Lj^*$ as precisely the termwise exact module pullback $\overline G$. Thus these functors are the displayed $j_!$ and $j^*$ on the full ordinary unbounded derived categories. The construction uses neither constructibility nor finite Tor amplitude.

tool_uses.why: Exact additive module inverse image for an immersion establishes exactness of open restriction; no closed-unit node supplies this generic site tool.
Generic additive adjunction on complexes supplies the unit and counit before localization; the closed-unit route has no separate complexes construction.
Generic characterization of the induced exact functors as derived functors identifies the ordinary derived operations.
The exact termwise functors must first factor through quasi-isomorphism localization to define the ordinary derived functors.
Localization descent and equality detection provide the derived unit and counit and their triangle identities.
The already proved sheaf-level open extension adjunction supplies the input Hom bijection; this closed-unit item does not reprove that open-triangle lemma.
Defines the ordinary derived module pullback for any identified ring sheaves, covering every finite commutative ring rather than only A_{E,n}.
